claims.text: Y2O3 nanoparticles are stable oxide nanoparticles in the proposed refractory high-entropy alloy environment.
Introducing 1–3 vol% Y2O3 nanoparticles will improve the radiation tolerance of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The Y2O3 intervention will preserve the mechanical integrity of the refractory high-entropy alloy.
The Y2O3 intervention will preserve engineering practicality.
Controlled powder metallurgy can produce a uniform dispersion of 1–3 vol% fine Y2O3 nanoparticles in the alloy.
The dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will be located both at grain boundaries and within grain interiors.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as sinks for irradiation-induced point defects and small defect clusters.
The Y2O3 defect sinks trap or promote recombination of irradiation-induced defects.
Y2O3 nanoparticles reduce the mobility and coalescence of irradiation-induced defects.
Reduced defect mobility and coalescence mitigate radiation-damage accumulation.
The proposed defect-sink mechanism reduces irradiation-induced void swelling.
The proposed defect-sink mechanism reduces irradiation-induced dislocation-loop formation.
The Y2O3 dispersion does not significantly compromise the matrix's intrinsic strength.
The Y2O3 dispersion does not significantly compromise the matrix's ductility.
After irradiation, Y2O3-containing samples will have a lower defect density than identically irradiated unmodified samples.
After irradiation, Y2O3-containing samples will exhibit a statistically significant reduction in irradiation-induced hardening relative to the unmodified baseline.
After irradiation, Y2O3-containing samples will exhibit a statistically significant reduction in void formation relative to the unmodified baseline.
The beneficial effect is expected to hold for 1–3 vol% Y2O3 under irradiation temperatures and regimes typical of plasma-facing fusion service.
Extreme irradiation regimes or excessive Y2O3 content may eliminate the beneficial effect.
